faqs.a: Blending mixes the red, green and blue channels separately, which is fast and predictable. Blending in HSL or LAB can look more natural for some pairs, but RGB is the standard behavior most tools use, and its results are easy to reason about.

faqs.a: At 50%, red (255, 0, 0) and blue (0, 0, 255) average to (127.5, 0, 127.5), which rounds to (128, 0, 128) — purple, #800080. That is the classic midpoint.
faqs.q: What is the midpoint of red and blue?

color-blender.formula:
result channel = A x (1 - t) + B x t, where t = ratio/100
applied separately to the red, green and blue channels
t = 0 gives pure A, t = 1 gives pure B
howTo: Pick color A and color B with the color pickers or type HEX codes.
Move the ratio slider toward the color you want to dominate.
Watch the large preview and read the resulting HEX and RGB values.
Click Copy to place the blended HEX code on your clipboard.
Paste it into your CSS or design tool.
keyFacts: Blending averages the red, green and blue channels of two colors.
A 50% ratio gives the exact midpoint between the two colors.
At 0% you get pure color A; at 100% you get pure color B.
Each channel rounds to the nearest whole number (0-255) before HEX conversion.
The result is also shown as a large live preview swatch.

color-blender.workedExample:
Blend pure red #ff0000 with pure blue #0000ff at 50%.
t = 50/100 = 0.5.
Red channel: 255 x 0.5 + 0 x 0.5 = 127.5, rounds to 128.
Green channel: 0 x 0.5 + 0 x 0.5 = 0.
Blue channel: 0 x 0.5 + 255 x 0.5 = 127.5, rounds to 128.
Result: rgb(128, 0, 128) = #800080 — the classic purple midpoint.
